name: typed-pointer-graph

protocol.note: One load_ref over a 16-byte allocation (never read on the GPU in this lowering) plus one store_via targeting a separate 4-byte allocation via ref_operand, covered by a single declared_pointer_edges entry. load_via/store_via's target is statically resolved host-side in ir::verify() before compile() runs, so compile() reports the compute_package event CachedObject rather than Direct (ADR-028).

correctness.oracle: reference::execute (dynamic dangling-ref check: loaded PointerRef must match the dereferencing instruction's own {allocation, generation}) plus compute_package.cpp's store_word_pattern byte-broadcast
correctness.tolerance: exact (report classification is an exact enum match; store_via's written bytes must exactly equal the byte-broadcast pattern of the stored value)

judgement: compiler::build_pointer_graph_compute_package (ADR-028) gives E002 a real Metal + reference result under a CachedObject lowering: load_ref is elided from the generated kernel entirely (its value is never read on the GPU in this lowering, only by the reference executor's dynamic dangling-ref check), and load_via/store_via targets are bound by static binding(N) index -- their identity is already resolved host-side via ir::Module::declared_pointer_edges, checked in ir::verify() before compile() ever runs, so no dynamic GPU-side pointer chase is needed. This is a deliberate divergence from the original plan's Vulkan framing (a real BDA-based device-pointer dereference) applied identically on both backends: building a host-side allocation-id -> device-address table would be disproportionate infrastructure for targets that are already statically known. Metal wiring required fixing two self-detected latent bugs before they could ship: Impl::ensure_pipeline's hardcoded kernel function name (would have failed pipeline creation for every pointer-graph module) and submit()'s ir::Access classification ternary defaulting load_ref/load_via/store_via to Publish (would have silently mis-tagged every pointer-graph instruction's trace/witness entry). Both fixed and verified via vertical-slice.metal.pointer-graph on real Apple Silicon hardware.
vulkan_status: compile-review-only (ADR-024); vulkan_device_hal.cpp still calls build_linear_compute_package unconditionally and would reject a pointer-graph module exactly as Metal would have pre-B15 -- a documentation-only comment block above DeviceHal::compile maps the same CachedObject-only design (not the plan's originally-envisioned real BDA pointer-chase) onto this backend's existing buffer_reference push-constant convention, with zero functional change (ADR-028)
